symbols.name: fixed space
symbols.meaning: The fixed space in which all labels lie.
symbols.quote: Fix a space $V$ of dimension $m$; $m$ counts the independent directions in $V$, and every label lies in $V$.

symbols.name: space dimension
symbols.meaning: The dimension of V, which counts the independent directions in V.
symbols.quote: Fix a space $V$ of dimension $m$; $m$ counts the independent directions in $V$, and every label lies in $V$.

symbols.name: vertex label
symbols.meaning: The subspace of V assigned to a vertex.
symbols.quote: A label is a subspace $L(x) \subseteq V$ attached to each vertex $x$ of the network, where a vertex is a gate or terminal.

symbols.name: vertex
symbols.meaning: A gate or terminal of the network, at the tail of an edge.
symbols.quote: A label is a subspace $L(x) \subseteq V$ attached to each vertex $x$ of the network, where a vertex is a gate or terminal.

symbols.name: neighbouring vertex
symbols.meaning: The vertex at the other end of an edge from x.
symbols.quote: Along an edge from $x$ to $y$, the labels are nested: one is contained in the other.

relations.quote: Labels are unaffected by a change of [Frame of a vertex](frame.md) along an edge, because such changes cancel between the two ends of a route.
The construction is built from a [Subset-intersection finite network](subset-network.md) on three-element subsets, whose gather and scatter wires create coefficients that depend on intersection size.
